Record real examples. Build a small model for your signing style.

Each sign-language profile uses separate recordings. Use a sign you know, or learn it from a fluent signer.

Record varied resting hands and unrelated movements as background. These examples are never spoken.

2. Record & train

Choose a sign to record

3-second countdown · 2.2-second recording

At least 3 independent examples per sign and 3 background examples are required.

A personal model learns your examples. It has no measured accuracy until you test on new recordings. Vary position, timing, lighting and recording sessions.

SOUND LIKE YOURSELF

Voice & settings.

Choose a voice, set your pace, and control what stays on your device.

Speech output

Voice language changes pronunciation, not translation. Set a sign’s spoken words in the selected spoken language. Available languages depend on installed system voices.

Recognition & privacy

Applies to the pretrained ASL “I love you” classifier. Personal models use distance and class separation.

Off by default. Recordings and settings are saved locally. Camera frames are used for inference and then discarded. Browser/OS speech services may use network synthesis.

Use the app offline

Optional. Download the app shell; dictionaries and camera assets are cached after their first use. Source videos require their provider connection.

Camera access needs HTTPS or localhost. The tracking model is bundled with this app. Browser and operating-system voices vary; Hindi may need an installed voice.
SMALL STEPS. REAL CONNECTION.

Let’s get started.

An honest prototype, with room to grow.

01

Try the ASL starter

Enable the camera in ASL mode. For the ASL “I love you” handshape, extend your thumb, index finger and little finger; fold the middle and ring fingers. Hold the pose for a moment.

This uses a pretrained MediaPipe gesture classifier. Other generic gestures are not converted into sign-language words.

02

Train ISL or more ASL signs

Choose a language in Teach a sign. Add a sign, record at least three full examples, then record a neutral/background class. Train the selected language and try it on camera.

ISL starts with an empty vocabulary: there is no bundled pretrained ISL translator. Ask a fluent signer to verify labels and examples.

03

See it. Check it. Speak it.

Recognized signs enter your message. Review or edit it and select Speak message. Auto-speak is optional and off by default. Lower your hands or pause before repeating the same sign.

English/Hindi speech uses available device voices and the words you assign. It does not translate text automatically.

What the model can—and cannot—do

This version recognizes a limited set of isolated signs, using two-hand landmarks and temporal example matching. Its personal match score is a similarity heuristic, not a probability of correctness. Face expressions, body posture and sign grammar are not modeled.

It cannot reliably translate unrestricted continuous signing or generalize to new signers. ISL and ASL are distinct languages. Concatenating recognized labels is not grammatical translation. Training and evaluation need representative recordings, fluent-signer review and explicit consent.
